tools.name: retrieve_context
tools.description: START HERE for a PostgreSQL question. Hybrid search of every list (inbox narrows it) returned as cited passages within token_budget: one per thread, the author's own words (~1200 chars) with url, inbox, message_id, from, date. found=false with a reason when the archive does not discuss it. Write the answer yourself; cite each passage url. author/since/until: one person in a date window. Takes search operators; complete=false when out of budget_ms. A commit SHA returns the mail referring to it. For "why was X added/changed/reverted" it may add commit_context: the commit the question resolved to (resolved_by, matched), its message, states_reason (a rule's guess) and up to 4 sentences from its Discussion: threads; check it is the right commit. What a person said or objected to: said.

inbox.description: all (default), a list, or several comma-separated

since.description: On or after: YYYY[-MM[-DD]], ISO, or 2w/6m/1y ago

tools.name: animal_history
tools.description: One animal's runs, newest first; branch and since filter.

tools.name: animal_owner_contributions
tools.description: Animals one owner runs (owner_name or owner_email; at least one): the branches each tracks, last status, first_seen_at and days since.

tools.name: blame_symbol

tools.name: browse_by_date
tools.description: Threads active in a date range [since, until) on one list.

tools.name: build_status_freshness

tools.name: buildfarm_overview
tools.description: Buildfarm health: animal count, recent runs, failing animals, top owners, OS / branch breakdown, freshness.

tools.name: check_upstream_status

tools.name: code_index_status

tools.name: codebase_map

tools.name: commit_buildfarm_status

tools.name: commit_history
tools.description: Everything linked to one commit: subject, author, date, sha, message, the Discussion: thread (participants as people and organizations), commitfest entry, Discord mentions; for postgres also first_releases (per branch: sha, release or null, first_version, shipped), reverted_by and reverts. No diff (git_diff, git_show_file).

tools.name: commitfest_stats

tools.name: contribution_summary

tools.name: detect_changes
tools.description: The symbols that changed between two commits (file content hashes).

tools.name: discussion_links
tools.description: A commit's Discussion / Closes / Fixes / Backpatch-through trailers: raw text and URL. For the mail itself: git_search mail_refs.

tools.name: embedding_status
tools.description: Embedding coverage of a list: messages embedded, model, last run.

tools.name: entry_branches
tools.description: Repository branches tracked for a commitfest entry: repo, branch_name, is_authoritative.

tools.name: entry_history
tools.description: An entry's status across commitfests, matched by shared thread Message-ID (precise), else by title prefix (weak).

tools.name: find_breaks
tools.description: Animals that failed on a branch between two commits, by run time (the buildfarm has no commit order).

tools.name: find_contributions
tools.description: One person's contribution rows: commit SHAs and animals, each with role and release. By email, else name.

tools.name: find_dead_code
tools.description: Functions and methods nothing calls (no incoming call edges).

tools.name: find_entries_for_author
tools.description: Commitfest entries a person authored: email (exact) or name (substring, case-sensitive).

tools.name: find_entries_for_thread
tools.description: Commitfest entries whose page links any message of the thread.

tools.name: find_entries_with_failures_on
tools.description: An animal's recent failed runs, and commitfest entries failing in cfbot on branches it tracks (correlated by branch and time, not joined).

tools.name: find_failing_patches
tools.description: Entries whose latest cfbot build fails on a platform: cf_id, title, entry_status, needs_rebase (newest version does not apply), commitfest_number.

platform.description: linux, macos, windows, freebsd, netbsd, openbsd

tools.name: find_failing_runs
tools.description: The newest failing buildfarm runs fleet-wide: what is broken now.

since.description: Runs started at or after (RFC 3339; default 24h ago)

tools.name: find_passing_long_pending
tools.description: Entries green on every platform that apply to master, not updated for min_days: why isn't it committed?

tools.name: find_patches_by_platform_status
tools.description: Entries passing on one platform and failing on another (e.g. linux vs macos: a portability bug).

failing_on.description: Platform it fails on, e.g. macos

passing_on.description: Platform it passes on, e.g. linux

tools.name: find_pattern
tools.description: Regex search of code symbol bodies (trigram-indexed).

tools.name: find_rebase_needed_patches
tools.description: Entries cfbot says no longer apply to master: they need a rebase.

tools.name: find_related_discussions
tools.description: Mail related to a commit, topic or PR. A postgres SHA: the mail referring to it (how_it_refers). Else a substring of subjects and Message-IDs, falling back to semantic search.

query.description: Subject words, Message-ID substring or commit SHA

tools.name: find_similar_messages
tools.description: Messages near one message by embedding: related or duplicate threads.

tools.name: get_animal
tools.description: One animal: hardware, OS, compiler, owner, branches, last status, its last 20 runs.

tools.name: get_attachment
tools.description: One attachment, whole, by 1-based index or filename substring. Text as text (a .patch applies with git apply), binary as base64; size = decoded bytes; url. Large text: start_line/end_line, 2000 lines a call (total_lines, cut).

end_line.description: Text: last line, at most start_line + 1999

tools.name: get_author_messages
tools.description: One list's messages from a sender (name or address, as search's f:), newest first; since/until bound them.

since.description: On or after: YYYY[-MM[-DD]] or 2w/6m/1y ago

tools.name: get_callees
tools.description: What a symbol calls or references (forward call graph).

tools.name: get_callers
tools.description: Who calls or references qualified_name, with file and lines. HEAD only; macros and function pointers are not followed.

tools.name: get_commitfest
tools.description: One commitfest: entries by status and its top authors.

tools.name: get_communities
tools.description: Louvain clusters of the call graph: related symbols by functional area.

tools.name: get_community
tools.description: One community and its symbols.

tools.name: get_contributor
tools.description: A contributor by email (exact) or name (substring): canonical name, page hash, per-release counts by role, the 5 latest credited commits, animals owned. Cite https://pg.ddx.io/community/<hash>.

tools.name: get_contributor_history
tools.description: Every list message from a sender (address or name).

tools.name: get_dependents
tools.description: Transitive dependents: the blast radius if this symbol changes.

tools.name: get_doc_page
tools.description: One docs page as text: url, path, body, fetched_at. Find the path with search_docs; cite the url.

tools.name: get_entry
tools.description: One commitfest entry: title, status, commitfest, authors, reviewers, committer, mail threads, branches.

tools.name: get_execution_flows
tools.description: Execution paths through the call graph from entry points.

tools.name: get_impact
tools.description: Impact of changing a symbol: risk level, blast radius, communities and flows affected.

tools.name: get_inbox_info
tools.description: A list's name, addresses, message_count (a cross-post counts on each list) and last activity.

tools.name: get_inbox_stats
tools.description: A list's message counts per period, top authors, trends; total_messages; oldest_date/newest_date skip unparsable or impossible dates.

tools.name: get_inbox_summary
tools.description: One list: total messages, top 10 posters, threads, date range, average messages per day over its life.

tools.name: get_message
tools.description: One message: headers, in_reply_to/references, body (own words: quotes, forwards, inline patches, signature removed; full_text=true for all), attachments [{index, filename, content_type, size}], has_patch. quotes: own_words/in_message verdicts per quote (include_body=false: verdicts only). Raw: get_attachment, get_raw_message.

include_llm.description: Default false: each message's llm_estimate (see llm_estimate)

quotes.description: Up to 20 quotes to check (12+ chars)

tools.name: get_message_headers
tools.description: A message's headers as key/value pairs, all or one.

tools.name: get_message_references
tools.description: A message's references: References/In-Reply-To and Message-IDs in its body, each looked up in the archive.

tools.name: get_new_messages
tools.description: Messages after an article-number cursor, to poll without rescanning: after=0 first, then the returned last_article_num.

tools.name: get_patch_branches
tools.description: Git branches made from a pull request's patch series.

tools.name: get_patch_build_history
tools.description: One entry's cfbot build matrix: per job status, platform, config, log URL, at, started_at, seen_at; rollup: last_build_at, seen_at, passing/failing_platforms, applies_cleanly, needs_rebase (the newest patch does not apply; builds are of the last that did).

tools.name: get_patch_series
tools.description: Every iteration of a pull request posted to the lists.

tools.name: get_raw_message
tools.description: A message's raw RFC 822 bytes.

tools.name: get_repo_sync_stats
tools.description: A repository's commit cadence (median interval, suggested poll) and fetch log.

tools.name: get_repository_summary
tools.description: One repository: commits, top 10 contributors, branches, languages (indexed symbols), most-touched paths (sampled).

tools.name: get_signature
tools.description: A symbol's signature and doc comment.

tools.name: get_source_info
tools.description: One list_sources source: kind, item_count, last_update, next_sync, freshness_status, description; a postgresql.org list also has poll (p_new, due, next_poll).

kind.description: inbox, repository, docs, wiki, discord or legacy (for a shared name)

tools.name: get_symbol
tools.description: A symbol by qualified name: source, signature, docs, file location.

tools.name: get_tests_for
tools.description: Test symbols that reference a symbol.

tools.name: get_thread
tools.description: The reply thread of a message (what In-Reply-To/References join to it), oldest first; root_message_id is its first message. grouping=subject: the whole subject thread, as the /m/ page shows it (may hold several reply threads). Each message: from, to, cc, date, message_id, body (own words; full_text=true for all), attachments, has_patch. Pages of 20 (limit max 500; next_offset, has_more); bodies cut at max_body_chars. include_body=false: outline.

include_llm.description: Default false: each message's llm_estimate (see llm_estimate)

tools.name: get_thread_references
tools.description: A thread's cross-reference graph: Message-IDs cited in its bodies and the threads they point to.

tools.name: get_wiki_history
tools.description: A wiki page's revisions.

tools.name: get_wiki_page
tools.description: One wiki.postgresql.org page by title ("Don't Do This"): latest revision, author, date. Cite https://wiki.postgresql.org/wiki/<title>.

tools.name: git_analyze_activity
tools.description: Commits per period: development pace.

tools.name: git_analyze_authors
tools.description: Per author: commits, first and last date; by commit count.

tools.name: git_analyze_bus_factor
tools.description: Files with the fewest distinct authors (knowledge silos).

tools.name: git_analyze_churn
tools.description: Most often changed files.

tools.name: git_analyze_coupling
tools.description: File pairs often changed together (hidden dependencies).

tools.name: git_analyze_hotspots
tools.description: Churn per directory: the most changed areas.

tools.name: git_blame
tools.description: A file's commit history (git log <rev> -- <path>), newest first: sha, commit_id, author, date, summary, status. Not per-line blame (blame). Renames not followed.

tools.name: git_diff
tools.description: Range mode (head_branch, optional base_branch: commits in head not base, filtered by author/message/path) or diff mode (from_commit, to_commit: unified diff).

from_commit.description: Diff mode: from. Any commit form

tools.name: git_log
tools.description: Commit history like git log, newest first; path, author (substring), since/until, branch (branch, tag or major) filter. Each: sha, commit_id, message, author, dates; has_more.

tools.name: git_search
tools.description: Commit messages (or paths: search_in=paths) by keywords, best match first; every word, case-insensitive. Each commit: sha, commit_id, branch, branches (its branch, then its back-patches': a back-patched fix appears once per branch, so pick by branch), first_release (first final release on its branch containing it, or null), message, author, date, people, mail_refs (up to 5, with how_it_refers). A SHA or 7+ hex prefix returns that commit.

tools.name: git_show_file
tools.description: A file at any commit (git show <rev>:<path>); an unknown rev or path is an error. Max 2000 lines a call (start_line/end_line; total_lines, cut). Returns sha and ref.

tools.name: history-of
tools.description: For CI: given a diff, path, symbol, subject or feature, the most relevant default-branch commits, their mail discussion and the people involved.

repository.description: Its default branch is traced (default postgres)

tools.name: hybrid_search
tools.description: Mailing-list search, BM25 over own words and semantic, blended per thread; every list unless inbox narrows it. Up to limit threads, best first, each its best message: inbox, message_id, subject, from, date, thread_id, fused_score (0-1), similarity, excerpt. author/since/until: one sender in a date window. Takes search operators (operators, warnings, skipped report them); complete=false when out of budget_ms. A commit SHA returns the mail referring to it (how_it_refers).

inbox.description: all (default), a list, or several comma-separated

query.description: Words or a question; search's operators

since.description: On or after: YYYY[-MM[-DD]], ISO, or 2w/6m/1y ago

tools.name: hybrid_search_code
tools.description: Code search by keyword and meaning, fused (RRF). Needs embeddings.

tools.name: list_animals
tools.description: Buildfarm animals by OS, branch, last status or owner; failing first, then by name.

tools.name: list_branches
tools.description: A repository's branches: head commit, default.

tools.name: list_commitfests
tools.description: Commitfests: status (open / in-progress / closed) and entry counts by status.

tools.name: list_contributors
tools.description: Contributors from git trailers, author/committer headers and animal owners, most contributions first.

source.description: git, buildfarm, email, wiki or commitfest

tools.name: list_discord_channels
tools.description: Monitored Discord channels and their message counts.

tools.name: list_doc_versions
tools.description: Documentation versions and page counts.

tools.name: list_entries
tools.description: Commitfest entries (patch series) by status, commitfest or topic; paged.

tools.name: list_inboxes
tools.description: Every list: name, message_count, latest_message_date, latest_import_date, listid, description.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: Projects linking a forge repository to a list.

tools.name: list_recent
tools.description: A list's newest messages.

tools.name: list_repositories
tools.description: Every repository: name, branch, commit_count, file_count, symbol_count, latest_commit, last_fetched_at, import_state.

tools.name: list_sources
tools.description: Every source (inbox, repository, docs, wiki, discord): item count, last update, freshness. The names other tools take.

kind.description: inbox, repository, docs, wiki or discord

tools.name: list_threads
tools.description: A list's recent threads: message counts, date ranges, latest message.

tools.name: llm_estimate
tools.description: P(LLM wrote it) for one message: its text (element message) and, per patch it carries, the commit message and the code. Each element: p_llm, model_version, model_quality, heldout_auc, computed_at; null p_llm with a reason when not scored (never 0) or when the model's heldout_auc is below 0.6. At most 3 patches per message; mail received before 2022-11-30 is 0 by rule, with one commit_message and one code element however many patches it carries. Weak estimates, not verdicts: read the caveat.

tools.name: recent_commitfest_activity
tools.description: Entries updated since a cutoff, with a status histogram.

tools.name: search_commitfest
tools.description: Full-text search of commitfest entries (title, then people), the current commitfest unless commitfests; "phrase", -term, or. Each: cf_id, title, status, commitfest(s), people, last update, patch url, thread link, outlook (P(commit) or null). Operators: intitle:, from:, after:/before:, /regex/, commitfest:, release:. A commit SHA returns its threads' entries.

sort.description: Default relevance; likely/unlikely sort by P(commit)

tools.name: release_contributors
tools.description: Top contributors per role (authored, reviewed, tested, reported, committed) for one release, by distinct commits.

tools.name: repository_stats
tools.description: A repository's commits, files, branch and import state.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Keyword search of mail (BM25 over subject, sender, own words), every list unless inbox narrows it. Messages best first (collapse_threads: one per thread): inbox, message_id, subject, from, date, thread_id, excerpt; total, has_more. For exact words; questions: hybrid_search. complete=false: out of budget_ms or total is a lower bound. define:<term> adds definition.

collapse_threads.description: One hit per thread, the best (default false)

inbox.description: all (default), a list, or several comma-separated

query.description: Words. Operators: after:/before:, d:A..B, site:, from:, intitle:, intext:, to:/cc:, has:patch, link:, /regex/, -op; alone: newest first

since.description: On or after: YYYY[-MM[-DD]], ISO, or 2w/6m/1y ago

tools.name: search-regex
tools.description: POSIX-regex search of mail, optionally fuzzy (k edits per match). search's prefixes apply (s:, f:, t:, d:, b:).

tools.name: search_all_sources
tools.description: One search over docs, wiki and mail, by relevance; define:<term> adds definition.

query.description: Words or a question; search's operators

tools.name: search_discord_topics
tools.description: Discord conversations near a query: channel, approximate dates and participants only, never content or links (the Discord community agreement).

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: Full-text search of the docs ("phrase", -term, or), title first; the current release unless version(s). One result per page: title, path, url, versions, snippet. define:<term> (MVCC, T611, LATERAL) adds definition (glossary, SQL feature or key word). Operators: intitle:, inurl:, after:/before:. Read: get_doc_page.

tools.name: search_patches
tools.description: Patch series from [PATCH v2 3/7] subjects: version, number, total, series.

tools.name: search_patch_lines
tools.description: Which posted patches carry a line: the +/- lines of every patch posted to the lists, for an identifier, line or hunk. One entry per series (thread): first_version and latest_version carrying it (message_id, date, from, version, patch files with urls, matching lines), message count, and commit (the one that landed it via its Discussion: link, or null). Words match from a word start; any whitespace run matches; several lines must be in one file. complete=false (cut says why) at the read cap or budget.

query.description: Identifier, line or hunk (max 32 lines); a leading + or - names the side

tools.name: said
tools.description: What a person said, objected to or agreed with: rule-labelled stance sentences from their own words. author + topic ("what did Tom Lane object to in SIGFPE handling"), or message_id for one thread (every participant, or add author). Each: verbatim sentence, message_id, url, date, from, stance (opposes, concerned, supports, commits), cue, source (rule or commitfest status). Labels are a rule's guess: read the sentence. counts by stance; messages_read (max 400); complete=false when a cap or budget_ms cut it. Sentences without a cue word are not returned.

tools.name: list_skills
tools.description: The PostgreSQL agent skills published here: name, description, SKILL.md uri, files. Read one with load_skill.

tools.name: load_skill
tools.description: Read a skill: name gives SKILL.md and its file list; name + file one file; uri any skill:// document.

file.description: Another file of that skill, as load_skill lists it

tools.name: search_symbols
tools.description: C functions, macros, types and variables by name in HEAD (BM25, then fuzzy). Each: qualified_name, name, kind, language, file, start_line, end_line.

tools.name: search_wiki
tools.description: Full-text search of wiki.postgresql.org, current text unless history=true (per page its latest matching revision: rev_id, revision_url, author, comment, timestamp, is_current, matches). Operators as in search. A commit SHA returns the pages citing it.

since.description: With history: revisions at or after (YYYY-MM-DD or ISO-8601)

until.description: With history: revisions before the end of this date

tools.name: semantic_search
tools.description: Mail by meaning (embeddings), every list unless inbox narrows it; each result has inbox and an own-words excerpt.

inbox.description: all (default), a list, or several comma-separated

tools.name: semantic_search_code
tools.description: Code symbols by meaning. Needs embeddings.

tools.name: symbols_in_file
tools.description: A file's symbols in line order.

tools.name: regex_search_code
tools.description: Regex search of the CURRENT source only (HEAD), like git grep -E (^ $ per line). Files with repo_name, file_path, line_no, snippet. Other commits or history: code_search match=regex.

path_glob.description: SQL LIKE on the path, e.g. "%/src/backend/%.c"

tools.name: grep_repository
tools.description: Literal search of the CURRENT source only (HEAD), like git grep -F. Files with repo_name, file_path, line_no, snippet. Other commits or history: code_search.

tools.name: find_string_literals
tools.description: A literal in HEAD source, only inside "strings", after // or /* comments, or anywhere.

tools.name: upcoming_events
tools.description: PostgreSQL events in a date window: conferences, meetups, online events, CfP and registration deadlines, talks (speakers with person hash), releases, commitfests. Source: PostgreSQL Event Calendar (Andreas Scherbaum).

kind.description: event, cfp, deadline, session (a talk), release or signal

person.description: Person hash (8 hex): their talks only

where.description: Country, region (europe, north-america, ...), series slug, or online

tools.name: calendar_feeds
tools.description: Every calendar feed (iCalendar URL) with event counts: all, regions, countries, series, release cycle, teams, organisations.

tools.name: combine_calendars
tools.description: Several calendar feeds (from calendar_feeds; 1-200) as one subscription: hash, feeds, https and webcal urls; stable per selection.

tools.name: cross_reference
tools.description: What relates to one stored item. ref: Message-ID or URL, commit SHA or URL, docs URL or page, wiki URL or title, commitfest URL, CVE-YYYY-NNNNN, or feature:<words>. Related threads, commits (releases, reverted_by), docs, wiki pages, entries and people, each with why, strongest first; timeline (status and dated events) for a commit, thread, entry or feature; graph (design-history facts with confidence) for features and entries. ~3 s budget (late parts in timed_out). Same as GET /api/v2/related.

tools.name: whats_new
tools.description: Catch up: what a person or group did, and where they were named, in a window; newest first per kind. who: a name (fuzzy; close matches return ambiguous), email, hash:<8 hex>, team:<slug>, org:<name>, new:<window>, or a list. Kinds: waiting (one person, no topic: their open items, each with rule, priority 0-100, why, outlook, p_reply, p_more_replies; finished threads (a commit, a closed entry, a quiet thread, or a last message that only thanks or reports the work done: done_reason acknowledged / work_done) only counted in left_out unless done=show; a waiting thread whose last message laya estimates asks them nothing comes last with fold probably_not_waiting and its laya estimate), acted, mail_from, mail_to_cc, mail_mention, git_author, git_credit, git_mention, wiki_edit, wiki_mention, commitfest, calendar, roster. Names, hashes and urls, never addresses. ~4 s budget (late kinds in timed_out). Same as GET /api/v2/activity.

done.description: Finished waiting threads: hide (default) or show

during.description: Calendar event uid or url, or pg19: its dates

since.description: Date, 2w, today, pg19 or all (default 14 days ago)

topic.description: Narrows every kind by hybrid search, e.g. NUMA

tools.name: code_search
tools.description: The postgres source at any commit, or across history (code-history index, byte-exact). match: literal (default), regex (^ $ per line) or identifier (all spellings). Results name sha and ref. history (all, <rev>, A..B): every matching line any commit had, with the commits that added and removed it. complete=false: totals are lower bounds.

commit.description: Any commit form, a release (17.2) or <ref>@YYYY-MM-DD; default newest release branch

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: A postgres file at any commit (code-history index): numbered lines, at most 2000 a call (start_line/end_line); total_lines, complete; binary files return metadata.

commit.description: Any commit form, a release (17.2) or <ref>@YYYY-MM-DD; default newest release branch

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: Files under a directory at any commit (code-history index) with line counts; depth folds deeper paths; glob filters.

commit.description: Any commit form, a release (17.2) or <ref>@YYYY-MM-DD; default newest release branch

tools.name: blame
tools.description: Per-line blame of a postgres file at any commit, as git blame. ignore_revs skips pgindent commits (.git-blame-ignore-revs); reverse adds the commit that removed each line. Max 2000 lines a call. proposals=true: per line the earliest posted patch that added it. Not git_blame (a file's commit list).

commit.description: Any commit form, a release (17.2) or <ref>@YYYY-MM-DD; default newest release branch

tools.name: get_commit
tools.description: One postgres commit (code-history index): message, trailers (names only), Discussion threads, back-patch siblings, first_releases (per branch: sha, release such as 14.23 or null, first_version, shipped), reverted_by, reverts, posted_patch (the Discussion patch mail matching it best, score 0-1, or null), files with line counts, and the diff (max 3000 lines; diff_complete).

paths.description: Only diff files under these paths

tools.name: search_commits
tools.description: Postgres commits (code-history index), newest first, like git log. range: a rev (its first-parent line), A..B, or all (default: every branch; each commit once, branches = where its change landed). Filters: message, author (also credit trailers), paths, since/until, changed_lines (-G), occurrences (-S). complete=false when -G/-S matched over 300,000 lines.

tools.name: get_ontology
tools.description: What this server knows and which tool reads it: kinds of fact with attributes and counts, the design-history graph's relations, sources and confidence. Same as GET /api/v2/ontology.
